sentences: This bill would charge universities and colleges each year to help pay for the student loan system.
The charge would be a tax set by regulation, not by the bill itself.
The money would cover the government's costs of running the loan program, including data work and compliance checks.
changes: Imposes an annual tax on higher education providers.
Funds the Higher Education Loans Program and its administration.
Allows the charge amount to be set by regulation.
summary.affected: Higher education providers whose students can access HECS-HELP or FEE-HELP loans.

divisions.question: Higher Education Support (Charges) Bill 2019 and another - Second Reading - University funding

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2019-10-15.5.2) to agree with the bills' main idea. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bills for a [second time](https://www.peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/). The Senate can now discuss them in greater detail. ### What is the bills' main idea? According to the [bills digest](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd1920a/20bd003): > *Together, the [Charges Bill](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r6339) and the [Cost Recovery Bill](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r6338) propose to give effect to a 2018–19 Budget measure to introduce partial cost recovery arrangements for higher education providers whose students access the Higher Education Loan Program (HELP).* > > *These arrangements comprise two new charges:* > > * *an annual higher education provider charge to partially recover the cost of administering HECS‑HELP and FEE-HELP and* > * *an application fee to be paid by registered higher education providers seeking to become FEE‑HELP providers, to recover the cost of administering the FEE-HELP application process.*

speeches.speaker: Dan Tehan
speeches.brief: The Higher Education Support (Charges) Bill 2019 introduces an annual charge on higher education providers whose students use HECS-HELP or FEE-HELP, to partially recover Commonwealth administration costs. The charge amount will be set by regulations based on provider size, commencing 1 January 2020 with invoices issued in May 2021 after enrolment data reconciliation.

speeches.speaker: Dan Tehan
speeches.brief: The bill introduces an application fee for new higher education providers and an annual charge on existing providers to recover the costs of administering the HELP loan programs, effective from 1 January 2020, with an estimated $11.7 million in savings over four years.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Labor supported the higher education cost-recovery bills but moved an amendment to record that the government has damaged higher education through billions in cuts, including a $134.8 million research cut, a $2.2 billion cut from capping undergraduate places, and an estimated 235,000 students missing out on university places by 2031. The party said the charges should be absorbed by universities and not passed on to students.

speeches.speaker: Patrick Gorman
speeches.brief: The speaker argued the government's cost-recovery fees on universities for HELP administration would worsen Australia's already high tertiary fees, and noted the expected savings of $11 million could instead fund the CapTel program. They cited that 140,000 fewer apprentices and 24.5% fewer TAFE enrolments have occurred since 2013, and that one in seven students report going without food.
